bib.title: LLaMA-Omni: Seamless Speech Interaction with Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: LLaMA-Omni: Seamless Speech Interaction with Large Language Models. Qingkai Fang, Shoutao Guo, Yan Zhou, Zhengrui Ma, Shaolei Zhang, Yang Feng (ICT/CAS). ICLR 2025, arXiv 2409.06666v2, 1 Mar 2025.

COVERAGE: All 91,892 chars were extracted, every page including appendices A-C and Tables 3-7, and the references were skimmed. About 25K chars of base64 `<latexit>` junk from Figure 2 were stripped, which left 67,172 chars of real text. The body is 10 pages. References run to page 15, the appendices to page 18. Nothing was skipped.

CLAIMS (ranked)

- The latency is 236 ms, not 226 ms. It is the minimum response latency, at Ω=10.
  - number: 236.18 ms total (206.03 ms LLM + 30.15 ms vocoder). GPT-4o's average audio latency is quoted as 320 ms.
  - setup: streaming scenario, latency measured on 1 NVIDIA L40 GPU, greedy decoding, InstructS2S-Eval.
  - quote: "LLaMA-Omni can achieve a minimum latency of 236ms (with Ω = 10), which is even lower than GPT-4o's average audio latency of 320ms."
  - where: p.8, §4.5. Abstract, intro and conclusion also say 236ms. Table 4, p.17.
- Training is cheap.
  - number: about 65 hours on 4 L40 GPUs (the abstract says "less than 3 days"). The training set is 200K samples. Both stages use batch size 32 and 3 epochs.
  - setup: stage 1 trains the adaptor and the LLM at peak LR 2e-5. Stage 2 trains only the speech decoder at 2e-4. Both use a cosine schedule with 3% warmup.
  - quote: "The entire training process takes approximately 65 hours on 4 NVIDIA L40 GPUs."
  - where: p.6, §4.1.
- LLaMA-Omni scores highest in the offline scenario (Table 2). ASR-WER is worse than the cascaded systems and better than SpeechGPT.
  - number: S2TIF/S2SIF/∆/ASR-WER/UTMOS by model:
    - SpeechGPT: 2.98 / 2.19 / 0.79 / 45.00 / 3.8958
    - SALMONN+Orca: 3.44 / 3.40 / 0.04 / 3.78 / 3.8286
    - Qwen2-Audio+Orca: 3.47 / 3.38 / 0.09 / 6.77 / 3.6119
    - LLaMA-Omni: 3.99 / 3.47 / 0.52 / 10.82 / 3.9296
  - setup: InstructS2S-Eval, 199 instructions from AlpacaEval (helpful_base and vicuna subsets, math and code removed). The text is scored 1-5 by GPT-4o. Speech responses are first transcribed by Whisper-large-v3. Greedy decoding.
  - quote: "LLaMA-Omni 3.99 3.47 0.52 10.82 3.9296"
  - where: p.7, Table 2.
- The authors give two reasons for the S2TIF lead. The baselines are not aligned to speech style: they produce formatted content and redundant explanations. Their explanation for the higher WER is that the speech decoder saw only about 1K hours of data.
  - number: none beyond the 1K hours.
  - quote: "LLaMA-Omni's speech decoder is trained on only approximately 1K hours of data, which is far less than the industrial TTS model."
  - where: p.8.
- Chunk size Ω trades latency against quality (streaming sweep, Table 4). A larger Ω gives slightly lower ChatGPT score, better ASR-WER, better UTMOS and an almost constant speech rate.
  - setup: Ω in {10, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100} units. Total latency is LLM + vocoder.

| Ω | Total latency (ms) | ChatGPT | ASR-WER | UTMOS | WPS |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 | 236.18 | 3.54 | 9.84 | 3.2304 | 2.76 |
| 20 | 281.41 | 3.56 | 9.91 | 3.4748 | 2.75 |
| 40 | 346.73 | 3.52 | 10.37 | 3.6688 | 2.74 |
| 60 | 412.06 | 3.52 | 10.47 | 3.7549 | 2.74 |
| 80 | 487.44 | 3.50 | 10.70 | 3.7858 | 2.73 |
| 100 | 562.81 | 3.49 | 10.71 | 3.8242 | 2.74 |
| Offline | 1753.77 (1542.71 LLM + 211.06 vocoder) | 3.47 | 10.82 | 3.9296 | 2.73 |

  - quote: "At a latency of 563ms (Ω = 100), the results of all metrics are relatively close to those in the offline scenario."
  - where: p.8-9, Table 4 p.17.
  - Note that the ASR-WER in the streaming rows (9.84-10.71) is lower than offline (10.82).
- Cascaded streaming TTS degrades at low latency. Word-chunk size Θ in {1,3,5,7,9}. Both cascades can go below 300 ms, with the lowest latency at Θ=1.
  - number (Tables 6, 7, Θ=1): SALMONN+Orca is 232.16 ms, ChatGPT 3.28, WER 6.64, WPS 1.86 (offline 3.40 / 3.78 / 3.31). Qwen2-Audio+Orca is 308.61 ms, ChatGPT 2.79, WER 25.25, WPS 1.90 (offline 3.38 / 6.77 / 3.30). Qwen2-Audio+Orca's 308.61 ms at Θ=1 is above 300, and the text says "below 300ms", so the text is slightly loose.
  - quote: "streaming speech synthesis at the word level tends to introducing additional errors" and "when the latency is low, the overall speech rate of cascaded systems drops sharply."
  - where: p.9, Tables 6-7 p.18.
- SpeechGPT is far slower: more than 4.5 s in streaming. In Table 5 the streaming latency is 4929.65 ms at Ω=10, rising to 8366.83 ms at Ω=100 and 18090.45 ms offline. Streaming ChatGPT scores are 2.16-2.22 and ASR-WER is 42-45.
  - setup: chain-of-modality decoding generates the text instruction, then the text response, then units.
  - quote: "its decoding latency is significantly higher than other systems (>4500ms)"
  - where: p.9, Table 5.
- Offline baseline latencies (the whole response is generated before speech synthesis): LLaMA-Omni 1753.77 ms, SALMONN+Orca 5324.07 ms, Qwen2-Audio+Orca 9424.42 ms. This is Tables 4, 6, 7, where Table 6 is SALMONN+Orca and Table 7 is Qwen2-Audio+Orca.
- Human evaluation favours LLaMA-Omni.
  - number: wins/ties/losses out of 100 votes.
    - Helpfulness: vs Qwen2-Audio+Orca 50/20/30, vs SALMONN+Orca 48/28/24.
    - Naturalness: vs Qwen2-Audio+Orca 42/20/38, vs SALMONN+Orca 44/33/23.
  - setup: LLaMA-Omni at Ω=40 (347 ms) against SALMONN+Orca Θ=3 (352 ms) and Qwen2-Audio+Orca Θ=3 (420 ms). 20 random instructions, 5 participants, 100 votes per comparison.
  - quote: "each pairwise model comparison results in a total of 100 votes."
  - where: p.9, Fig 4. The text refers to it as "Figure 5". The vote counts are read from the extracted Fig 4 text, whose row-to-baseline mapping is inferred from order (Qwen2-Audio on top).
- The InstructS2S-200K dataset.
  - number: 200K samples. About 50K are from Alpaca and about 150K are first-turn instructions from the first 150K UltraChat entries. 418 h of instruction speech, 1058 h of response speech. Averages: instruction 7.5 s, response 19.0 s, text instruction 21.7 and text response 39.5 (units not stated), unit sequence 553.6.
  - setup: Llama-3-70B-Instruct rewrites the instructions (fillers, numbers spelled out, brief) and generates concise responses with no lists or parentheses. Speech is synthesised with CosyVoice-300M-SFT (random male or female voice) for instructions and VITS trained on LJSpeech for responses.
  - quote: "Speech Instruction Duration 418h / Speech Response Duration 1058h"
  - where: p.5, Table 1.
- Architecture and configuration.
  - Whisper-large-v3 encoder, frozen.
  - Adaptor: 5× downsampling by concatenating frames.
  - LLM: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct.
  - Speech decoder: 2 LLaMA-style Transformer layers, 425M parameters, hidden 4096, 32 heads, FFN 11008, non-autoregressive, trained with CTC. Upsample factor λ=25.
  - Units: HuBERT, K-means with 1000 clusters, unit HiFi-GAN vocoder with duration predictor.
  - quote: "The speech decoder consists of 2 Transformer layers with the same architecture as LLaMA, with a hidden dimension of 4096, 32 attention heads, and a feed-forward network dimension of 11008, which contains 425M parameters."
  - where: p.6.
- Decoding speed. Because the speech decoder is non-autoregressive, generating text plus speech is about as fast as generating text alone. This is a claim without a measured number.
  - quote: "the decoding speed for generating both text and speech responses simultaneously is not significantly different from the speed of generating text response alone."
  - where: p.4.
- Small Ω hurts quality in two ways. UTMOS falls at small Ω because speech is cut into more segments, which adds discontinuities. The authors also speculate that the vocoder handles short unit sequences more reliably, because it is trained on short sequences.
  - where: p.8.

LIMITS
- Offline is the default; the abstract's headline latency is the best streaming setting only. At Ω=10 the speech is the least natural, with UTMOS 3.23 against 3.93 offline.
- There is no decoding-mode ablation beyond offline vs streaming and the Ω sweep. There are no ablations of the CTC decoder, the upsample factor λ, the two-stage training, or the data. Decoding is greedy only.
- The evaluation is small. InstructS2S-Eval is 199 text-synthesised instructions (CosyVoice), with no real human speech. The human study has 20 prompts and 5 raters. The judge is GPT-4o, and the S2SIF score depends on Whisper ASR. The authors concede the S2SIF drop comes partly from "errors introduced during the speech synthesis process and the reliance on an ASR model for evaluation".
- Latency is measured only on a single L40, and "latency" is time to the start of the speech response. No end-to-end audio-in-to-audio-out measurement with input streaming is given, and the model waits for the whole spoken instruction (not full-duplex).
- ASR-WER of 10.82 offline is worse than the cascaded systems (3.78, 6.77). The authors blame the small 1K-hour training set for the speech decoder. The voice is a fixed LJSpeech VITS voice, so the speech has no expressiveness. The future-work section lists "enhancing the expressiveness of generated speech responses and improving real-time interaction capabilities".
- Only English is evaluated, and only single-turn instructions: only the first turn of UltraChat is used.
- Baselines are SpeechGPT, SALMONN+Orca and Qwen2-Audio+Orca. Mini-Omni and Moshi are named only in related work and are not compared. This is dated by 2026.
- Related-work claim: the authors say they train on far less data than Mini-Omni and Moshi, and that unlike theirs, CTC removes the need to pre-align speech and text.

BUILDS ON
- SpeechGPT (Zhang et al., 2023): the discrete-unit target and the chain-of-modality baseline.
- Whisper (Radford et al., 2023): the encoder.
- Ma et al. (2024b): the speech adaptor, which downsamples by concatenating frames.
- Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Dubey et al., 2024): the LLM.
- HuBERT (Hsu et al., 2021): the units.
- Unit HiFi-GAN with duration predictor (Polyak et al., 2021; Kong et al., 2020): the vocoder.
- CTC (Graves et al., 2006a).
- NAR streaming Transformer (Ma et al., 2023), plus Ma et al. (2024a) and Zhang et al. (2024b) (StreamSpeech): the streaming decoder.
- Cho et al. (2024), "Speechworthy": concise answers for speech.
- Contemporaries: Mini-Omni (Xie & Wu, 2024) and Moshi (Défossez et al., 2024).

CODE
Algorithm 1, the inference loop (p.4). Streaming works by running the CTC decoder over the growing upsampled hidden states, collapsing the units, and flushing a chunk to the vocoder once at least Ω new units exist:
```
if |Y^U| - j >= Ω then
  y^S ← V(Y^U_{j+1:}); Y^S ← Y^S + y^S; j ← |Y^U|
```
Prompt template (App. A, p.16):
```
<|begin of text|><|start header id|>system<|end header id|>
You are a helpful language and speech assistant. You are able to understand the speech content that the user provides, and assist the user with a variety of tasks using natural language. <|eot id|>
<|start header id|>user<|end header id|>
<speech>
Please answer the questions in the user's input speech. <|eot id|>
<|start header id|>assistant<|end header id|>
```
Appendix A also gives three other prompts. One is the GPT-4o scoring prompt (1-5 on helpfulness, relevance, fluency and suitability for speech interaction, output as JSON). The other two are Llama-3-70B prompts for instruction rewriting and for response generation.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.2): simultaneous text and speech generation overview.
- Fig 2 (p.3): architecture and two-stage training. The extraction is garbled, so look at the image.
- Fig 3 (p.8): four latency-vs-metric curves (ChatGPT score, ASR-WER, UTMOS, WPS) for all systems, streaming and offline. This is the quickest view of LLaMA-Omni's latency-quality frontier against the cascades.
- Fig 4 (p.9): human-evaluation win/tie/lose bars for helpfulness and naturalness.
- I did not run the figure-caption script.

PROBLEMS
